advantages in cost, Habitable Structures, environmental impacts, river exposure, stream crossings,

recorded historical and archeological sites, Prudent Avoidance, and route-wide moderation in

order to move the Colorado River crossing incrementally farther south of two state parks.

       That trade-off is not supported by the full record.

        -    Maximize distance from residences (single-& multi-family).
        -    Maximize distance from schools.

B. Parks and Recreation Areas.

        1.       Reply Regarding Recreation Areas: The Colorado River Experience.

        The southern route proponents want to avoid using Link J22 to cross the Colorado River.

They use protecting the viewshed from the Colorado Bend State Park and Post Oak Ridge State

within 1,000 feet of Route 894’s centerline, and Route 894 has no right-of-way within the EA’s

defined foreground visual zone of a park or recreation area.27

        The contention that the park experience is damaged due to the possible visual impacts of

         2.       Reply Regarding Link J31 and Paralleling.

        Staten Creek Ranch, Cherokee Creek Aligned Intervenors, Save the Lampasas and the

K13/K51 Landowner briefs repeatedly reference the purported benefit of a pipeline when

discussing Link J31. Yet, as Ms. Perkins confirmed, pipelines are not compatible right-of-way.42

Moreover, the record shows that Link J31 does not “abut” a pipeline – it is at least 1,200 feet away

from a pipeline that was bored under the Colorado River.43 Applicants’ discovery responses

confirm that “paralleling” means routing two linear features so they are the same distance from

one another at any given point, and that the maximum distance of separation used to make

“paralleling” determinations was approximately “100 feet from the edge of the abutting right-of-

way.”44

        Here, Link J31 is not “paralleling” anything at the Colorado River. Ms. Reinecke admitted

that the pipeline “crossing” the Colorado River was actually bored under the Colorado River and

that the pipe ran “hundreds of feet below the top of [the] bluffs” located at the banks of the

Colorado River.45 She also confirmed that the pipeline began its descent 100-200 feet before it

even got to the river banks.46 Given this, it is highly questionable to charge the pipeline with

“disturbing” any particular location on the bluffs – much less at Link J31.47

          Going further, how a pipeline could have disturbed the bluffs at Link J31 when the

offending pipeline is underground and at least 1,200 feet away from Link J31 defies all logic.

Landowners, Carpenter Land and Cattle, and Staten Creek Ranch are really asking Applicants to

use a link that they prefer when crossing the Colorado River. But, as Russell Marusak and Brenda

Link J22 was the best link to use.54 Marusak and Perkins testified that they committed to not

fragmentation near Link J22.56 In light of these considerations, Route 894 was selected, which

utilizes Link J22 to cross the Colorado River, the link that Brenda Perkins identified as “most

favorable.”57 Because Applicants are the ones that are going to build this project, their analysis on

       The Yates Keith Alliance continues to support Route 894 as the Best Meets Route.

Applicants selected Route 894 after a holistic review of the study area, including environmental

selecting Route 894. The process helped identify additional recorded trinomials on Links G6 and

Il, including the Rose Ranch trinomial; confirmed field-surveyed golden-cheeked warbler habitat

and observed bird presence along Link J31; raised credible concerns regarding golden-cheeked
